mainTopic: Righteous people who received special gifts, the end of פרק השותפין, and the opening משנה on distances from a neighbor's wall
overview: The amud opens with a series of lists of very special righteous people. אברהם, יצחק and יעקב got a taste of עולם הבא in this world, and the יצר הרע had no power over them. Some say דוד also belongs on that second list, but the other opinion reads his פסוק as describing his suffering. A ברייתא lists six people who died by a divine kiss and not through the מלאך המות. The גמרא asks how מרים can be included, and רבי אלעזר answers with a גזירה שוה. A second ברייתא lists seven people whose bodies worms never touched, with an argument again about whether דוד is included. A third ברייתא lists four people who died only because of the נחש, with no sin of their own, and the גמרא proves ישי's place on that list from the words 'אביגיל בת נחש'. Then פרק השותפין ends. The new פרק opens with a משנה about how far a person must keep pits, materials, planting, a mill and an oven from a neighbor's wall.

steps.title: Three people got a taste of the World-to-Come
steps.stepSummary: אברהם, יצחק and יעקב were given a taste of עולם הבא in this world, based on the words בכל, מכל, כל.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Three people were given a taste in this world] of the World-to-Come: אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. About אברהם it says 'with everything,' about יצחק it says 'from everything,' and about יעקב it says 'everything.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started on the previous page: three people got a taste of עולם הבא while still alive. It brings a word from a פסוק for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three אבות has a פסוק that uses the word 'everything' (בכל, מכל, כל). Being blessed with 'everything' means having a complete, perfect blessing, and that perfection is a small taste of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A taste or sample of the World-to-Come
As it is written about him

phrases.english: a taste of the World-to-Come; they are:
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the previous page: 'Three people were given by הקב״ה a taste in this world...'

phrases.english: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Abraham, as it is written about him: 'with everything.'
Isaac, as it is written about him: 'from everything.'
Jacob, as it is written about him: 'everything.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, אֵלּוּ הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of teachings that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם, יצחק and יעקב tasted עולם הבא in this world, as shown by בכל, מכל, כל.

steps.title: Three people the evil inclination could not rule
steps.stepSummary: The same three אבות were not ruled by the יצר הרע, using the same three words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three people were not ruled by the evil inclination: אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, because it is written about them 'with everything,' 'from everything,' 'everything.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second list with the same three people and the same three פסוקים. This time the gift is that the יצר הרע had no power over them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words now teach something new. A person blessed with 'everything' has a complete blessing, and that includes not having to fight the יצר הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not rule over them / had no power over them

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה לֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן יֵצֶר הָרָע,
phrases.english: Three, over whom the evil inclination had no power;
they are: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob;
as it is written about them: 'with everything,' 'from everything,' 'everything.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה לֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן יֵצֶר הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new list that reuses the same people and פסוקים as step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע had no power over אברהם, יצחק and יעקב.

steps.title: Some add דוד המלך to the list
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says דוד was also free of the יצר הרע, based on 'my heart is empty within me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: דוד too, as it is written: 'And my heart is empty (dead) within me.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion adds דוד to the list of people the יצר הרע could not rule. It brings a פסוק from תהלים as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof reads 'my heart is empty' to mean the יצר הרע inside his heart was gone, as if that part of his heart had died. This sets up the next step, where the first opinion reads the פסוק differently.

phrases.english: And some say: David too,
as it is written: 'And my heart is empty within me.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 109:22. They read it as: the bad inclination in his heart was gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth name to the list in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the יש אומרים, דוד was also not ruled by the יצר הרע.

steps.title: The first opinion reads דוד's פסוק as describing pain
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that leaves out דוד explains that the פסוק is about his suffering, not about the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion? He is talking about his suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the first opinion, which leaves דוד out, deals with the פסוק. Its answer: דוד is only describing how much he suffered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the proof for adding דוד. 'My heart is empty within me' can describe a broken heart from pain, so it does not show the יצר הרע was gone.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (how does the other opinion explain it?)

phrases.english: And the other? It is his suffering that he is mentioning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof brought in step 3 from the side of the first opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסוק that דוד belongs on the list.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק can be read as describing emotional pain rather than the end of the יצר הרע.

steps.title: Six people the Angel of Death could not rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists six people who were not taken by the מלאך המות: the three אבות, plus משה, אהרן and מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Six were not ruled by the מלאך המות: אברהם, יצחק, יעקב, משה, אהרן and מרים. The אבות, because it says 'with everything, from everything, everything.' משה, אהרן and מרים, because it says they died 'by the mouth of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives a third list: six people whose death did not come through the מלאך המות. It gives two different sources, one for the אבות and one for משה, אהרן and מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the אבות, the 'everything' blessing means they were also spared the pain of the מלאך המות. For משה, אהרן and מרים, dying 'by the mouth of ה׳' is understood as dying with a divine kiss. This sets up the next question, because that phrase is not written about מרים.

keyTerms.meaning: By the mouth of ה׳ (understood as death by a divine kiss)

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה לֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Six, over whom the Angel of Death had no power,
and they are: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,
Moses, Aaron and Miriam.
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, as it is written about them:
'with everything,' 'from everything,' 'everything';

phrases.aramaic: מֹשֶׁה, אַהֲרֹן וּמִרְיָם – דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ: ״עַל פִּי ה׳״.
phrases.english: Moses, Aaron and Miriam, as it is written about them: 'by the mouth of the Lord.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 33:38 (אהרן); דברים 34:5 (משה). 'By the mouth of ה׳' means they died with a kiss from ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה לֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new list, brought from a ברייתא, that adds three people to the אבות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six people died without the מלאך המות: the three אבות, משה, אהרן and מרים.

steps.title: But the פסוק never says this about מרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: 'על פי ה׳' is never written about מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about מרים it is not written 'by the mouth of ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source the ברייתא gave for מרים. The phrase 'by the mouth of ה׳' appears with משה and אהרן, but not with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא grouped all three under one פסוק phrase. But the פסוק about מרים's death does not have those words, so it looks like there is no source for including her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not written about her

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִרְיָם לָא כְּתִיב בָּהּ: ״עַל פִּי ה׳״!
phrases.english: But about Miriam it is not written: 'by the mouth of the Lord'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִרְיָם לָא כְּתִיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given for מרים in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'על פי ה׳' is written about מרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about מרים's death does not contain the words 'על פי ה׳', so the stated source does not cover her.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: מרים died by a kiss, learned from משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says מרים also died with a kiss, learned through the word 'שם' that appears with both her and משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: מרים also died with a kiss, as we learn 'there' from 'there' from משה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge. Both פסוקים, about מרים and about משה, use the word 'שם' (there), so we connect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places links the two cases. Since משה died 'שם... על פי ה׳', מרים, who died 'שם', also died by a divine kiss even though it is not written openly.

keyTerms.meaning: For it is learned (from another place)
Learning from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Miriam also died with a kiss,
for it is learned 'there'–'there' from Moses.
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:1 says 'מרים died there'; דברים 34:5 says 'משה died there.' The shared word links them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִרְיָם נָמֵי בִּנְשִׁיקָה מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides a different source, a גזירה שוה, for including מרים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the words 'על פי ה׳', there seemed to be no source that מרים died by a kiss.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared word 'שם' links מרים to משה, so she also died by a kiss.

steps.title: Why the תורה did not say it openly about מרים
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'על פי ה׳' was left out for מרים because it would be unseemly to say it about a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was 'by the mouth of ה׳' not said about her? Because it is unseemly to say.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers a natural follow-up question: if מרים really died by a kiss, why didn't the Torah just say so? He explains that saying it openly would be improper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the gap left by step 7. The תורה hinted at it through the word 'שם' instead of writing 'by the mouth of ה׳', because describing a divine kiss for a woman would not be dignified.
steps.whatToRemember: Six people died without the מלאך המות. The אבות are learned from 'בכל, מכל, כל'. משה and אהרן are learned from 'על פי ה׳'. מרים is learned through the shared word 'שם' with משה, and the תורה did not state it openly out of dignity.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר בָהּ ״עַל פִּי ה׳״ –
phrases.english: And for what reason is 'by the mouth of the Lord' not said about her?
Because it is unseemly to say it.
phrases.notes: It wouldn't be proper to describe a kiss from ה׳ when speaking about a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר בָהּ ״עַל פִּי ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question raised by the answer in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the Torah hinted instead of stating openly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If מרים died by a kiss, the Torah should have written 'על פי ה׳' about her as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was left out because saying it openly about a woman would be unseemly.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מרים is included among those who died by a divine kiss; the Torah hinted at it only because of dignity.

steps.title: Seven people whose bodies worms never touched
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists seven people whose bodies were never eaten by worms: the three אבות, משה, אהרן, מרים, and בנימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: There were seven people that worms and maggots had no power over: אברהם, יצחק, יעקב, משה, אהרן, מרים, and בנימין the son of יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, similar to the earlier list of six who died with a kiss. This one lists seven people whose bodies stayed whole in the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא was about how they died (no מלאך המות). This one is about what happened to their bodies after death (no worms). The list is the same six people plus בנימין.

keyTerms.meaning: Worm and maggot, the creatures that eat a body in the grave
Had no control or power over
The Sages taught; this opens a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Seven, over whom there had no power
the worm and the maggot,
and these are they: Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
Moshe, Aharon and Miriam,
and Binyamin son of Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁבְעָה לֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן רִמָּה וְתוֹלֵעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that follows the earlier list of six who died with a kiss, now about protection from worms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven people's bodies were not touched by worms: the three אבות, משה, אהרן, מרים, and בנימין.

steps.title: The פסוקים behind each name on the list
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a פסוק source for each group: 'בכל, מכל, כל' for the אבות, 'על פי ה׳' for משה, אהרן and מרים, and 'ידיד ה׳ ישכן לבטח' for בנימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אבות, because about them it says 'with everything,' 'from everything,' 'everything.' משה, אהרן and מרים, because about them it says 'by the mouth of ה׳.' בנימין, because it says: 'To בנימין he said: the beloved of ה׳, he shall dwell securely by Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now shows where in the תורה we learn about each person on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reuses the same sources it gave for the list of six. The 'everything' blessing covers the אבות, and dying 'על פי ה׳' covers משה, אהרן and מרים. The only new source is for בנימין: 'he shall dwell securely' is read as resting safely even in the grave, untouched by worms.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With everything, from everything, everything': the words of blessing used for the three אבות
Beloved of ה׳, said about בנימין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not reopen the question from Steps 6-8. 'על פי ה׳' is not written about מרים, but we already learned she is included through the word 'שם'.

phrases.english: Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov:
as it is written [about them]:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: "with everything," "from everything," "everything."
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:1, 27:33, 33:11, one word for each of the three אבות.

phrases.english: Moshe, Aharon and Miriam:
as it is written [about them]: "by the mouth of ה׳."
Binyamin son of Yaakov:
as it is written: "And to Binyamin he said:
The beloved of ה׳, he shall dwell securely by Him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב – דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק sources for the list in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That each of the seven was protected from worms
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית (בכל, מכל, כל), the deaths 'על פי ה׳', and דברים 33:12

steps.title: Some add דוד to the list
steps.stepSummary: יש אומרים: דוד was also protected from worms, because he wrote 'my flesh also dwells securely.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: דוד too, as it is written: 'My flesh also dwells securely.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion adds an eighth person, דוד המלך, based on his own words in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ישכן לבטח' match the words used about בנימין in Step 10. So this opinion reads דוד's words the same way, as resting safely in the grave.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: a second opinion

phrases.english: And some say: David too,
as it is written: "My flesh also dwells securely."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a name to the list, using the same wording that was used for בנימין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the יש אומרים, דוד's body was also not touched by worms.

steps.title: The first opinion says דוד was only praying
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that leaves out דוד explains that 'אף בשרי ישכן לבטח' is a prayer for mercy, not a promise that came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion? That פסוק is דוד asking for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the first opinion explains the פסוק about דוד, and answers that דוד was only asking for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With בנימין, the פסוק is a blessing from משה, so it really happened. With דוד, the words are his own request, and a request does not prove it was granted. This is like Step 4, where the opinion leaving out דוד also read his פסוק differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does the other opinion explain it?
Mercy; here, a prayer asking for mercy

phrases.english: And the other opinion?
That is mercy that he is asking for.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – הָהוּא רַחֲמֵי הוּא דְּקָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the first opinion by taking away the proof of the יש אומרים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using תהלים 16:9 as proof that דוד was protected
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is a prayer, not a description of what happened

steps.title: Four people who died only because of the נחש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four people who never sinned and died only because of the נחש's advice in גן עדן: בנימין, עמרם, ישי, and כלאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Four people died only because of the advice of the נחש. They are: בנימין son of יעקב, עמרם father of משה, ישי father of דוד, and כלאב son of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about very special people, this time people with no sin of their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death came into the world because of the נחש's advice to חוה. These four had no personal sin that caused their death. They died only because all people became mortal after that first sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the advice of the נחש in גן עדן

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Four died
because of the advice of the snake.
phrases.notes: He means they died only because death entered the world through the נחש, not because of any sin of theirs.

phrases.english: And these are they: Binyamin son of Yaakov,
and Amram father of Moshe,
and Yishai father of David,
and Chilav son of David.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעָה מֵתוּ בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related ברייתא about extraordinary righteous people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בנימין, עמרם, ישי and כלאב died without sin, only because of the נחש.

steps.title: Only ישי is hinted at in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the other three are known by tradition, but ישי has a פסוק, which calls his daughter אביגיל 'בת נחש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them are known by tradition, except ישי father of דוד, whom a פסוק spells out: 'And אבשלום put עמשא over the army instead of יואב. עמשא was the son of a man named יתרא the Israelite, who came to אביגיל daughter of נחש, sister of צרויה, mother of יואב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how we know this list: three names come from tradition, and ישי comes from a פסוק. It quotes the פסוק to set up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'אביגיל בת נחש'. The proof is not complete yet. The next two steps will show why 'נחש' here must point to ישי.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a tradition handed down, not learned from a פסוק
That a פסוק spells out about him

phrases.english: And all of them are a tradition,
except for Yishai father of David,
about whom [a verse] spells it out,
as it is written: "And Avshalom placed Amasa
instead of Yoav over the army,
and Amasa was the son of a man
whose name was Yisra the Israelite,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּא אֶל אֲבִיגַיִל בַּת נָחָשׁ
phrases.english: who came to Avigayil daughter of Nachash,
sister of Tzeruyah, mother of Yoav."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ גְּמָרָא, לְבַר מִיִּשַׁי אֲבִי דָוִד דִּמְפָרַשׁ בֵּיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for one name on the list from Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That ישי died only because of the נחש

steps.title: But אביגיל was the daughter of ישי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can אביגיל be called 'בת נחש' when another פסוק shows she was the daughter of ישי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Was she the daughter of נחש? She was the daughter of ישי, as it is written: 'And their sisters were צרויה and אביגיל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the פסוק seems to contradict another פסוק about who אביגיל's father was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברי הימים, צרויה and אביגיל are listed as sisters of ישי's sons, so ישי was their father. So 'נחש' cannot be the name of a different father, and the word must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so? This opens a challenge
But is it not so that

phrases.english: But was she the daughter of Nachash?
Was she not the daughter of Yishai,
as it is written: "And their sisters were Tzeruyah and Avigayil"!
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:16. 'Their' means the sons of ישי listed just before.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בַּת נָחָשׁ הִיא? וַהֲלֹא בַּת יִשַׁי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a contradiction inside the proof that was just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'אביגיל בת נחש' in שמואל ב 17:25
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק shows that ישי was אביגיל's father, so 'נחש' cannot simply be her father's name.

steps.title: 'בת נחש' means daughter of the one who died because of the נחש
steps.stepSummary: The answer: אביגיל is called 'בת נחש' to teach that her father ישי died only because of the נחש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: the daughter of the one who died because of the advice of the נחש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction, and this finishes the proof for ישי from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls ישי 'נחש' on purpose, to hint that his only reason for dying was the נחש. So the contradiction is exactly what proves ישי belongs on the list.
steps.whatToRemember: ישי's place on the list comes from a פסוק: אביגיל is called 'בת נחש' even though her father was ישי. That teaches that ישי died only because of the נחש. The other three names come from tradition.

phrases.english: Rather, the daughter of one who died
because of the advice of the snake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בַּת מִי שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא and completes the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word: 'נחש' is a hint, not a name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בת נחש' means a man named נחש was אביגיל's father, which contradicts דברי הימים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בת נחש' means the daughter of the one (ישי) who died only because of the נחש.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק השותפין
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of בבא בתרא, השותפין, comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק השותפין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the first פרק. The topic is about to change to a new פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן line is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the פרק and a promise to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing words at the end of a פרק
The partners: the name of the first פרק of בבא בתרא

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The Partners"

steps.triggerLanguage: הַדְרָן עֲלָךְ הַשּׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק, including the אגדה that just finished.

steps.title: Do not dig a pit near a neighbor's pit without keeping a distance
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a person may not dig a pit, ditch, cave, water channel, or laundry pool near a neighbor's pit unless he keeps it three טפחים from the neighbor's wall and plasters it with lime.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not dig a pit close to his neighbor's pit, and not a ditch, a cave, a water channel, or a launderers' pool, unless he keeps it three טפחים away from his neighbor's wall and plasters it with lime.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about not damaging a neighbor's property. It lists kinds of water holes and the conditions for digging them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water and digging close by can weaken the ground and the wall of the neighbor's pit. So the משנה demands two things: a gap of three טפחים, and plaster to keep the water from seeping through. Without both, the digging is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A cave, meaning a pit with a roof
A launderers' pool for washing clothes
And he plasters it with lime

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the whole פרק about the distances a person must keep so that using his own property does not damage his neighbor's.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may not dig a pit
close to the pit of his fellow,
and not a ditch, and not a cave,
and not a water channel,
and not a launderers' pool,
unless he distanced it
from the wall of his fellow three handbreadths,
phrases.notes: The 'wall' here is the side wall of the neighbor's pit.

phrases.english: and he plasters with lime.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יַחְפּוֹר אָדָם בּוֹר סָמוּךְ לְבוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand new פרק and topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Digging a pit or similar water hole near a neighbor's pit requires a gap of three טפחים from his wall and plastering with lime.

steps.title: Keeping piles of materials away from a neighbor's wall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that olive refuse, manure, salt, lime, and rocks must be kept three טפחים from a neighbor's wall, or the wall must be plastered with סיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one must keep olive refuse, manure, salt, lime, and rocks three handbreadths away from his neighbor's wall, or plaster it with lime.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list. Now it names piles of materials that must be kept away from a neighbor's wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distance is three טפחים again, as in step 18. But the pit rule in step 18 demanded both the distance and plastering ('וסד בסיד'). Here the משנה says 'או סד בסיד', so plastering with סיד can replace the distance. The rule also now covers placing materials near the wall, not just digging. The משנה does not explain why these items matter; it only lists them.

keyTerms.meaning: One must keep at a distance
Olive refuse, the leftover pulp after pressing olives

phrases.english: And one must distance olive refuse, and manure,
phrases.notes: גפת is what's left after the oil is squeezed out of olives.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַמֶּלַח, וְאֶת הַסִּיד, וְאֶת הַסְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: and salt, and lime, and rocks,
from his neighbor's wall, three handbreadths;
or he plasters it with lime.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַרְחִיקִים אֶת הַגֶּפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of distancing rules, moving from dug-out spaces to piles of materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Olive refuse, manure, salt, lime, and rocks must be kept three טפחים from a neighbor's wall, or the wall must be plastered with סיד.

steps.title: Keeping seeds, plowing, and urine away from the wall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that seeds, a plow, and urine must be kept three טפחים from the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: One must keep seeds, the plow, and urine three handbreadths away from the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another group to the list: planting, plowing, and urine. Each must be kept three טפחים from the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distance is the same three טפחים as before. However, this clause does not mention the option of plastering with סיד. The items here are activities, planting and plowing, not only objects.

phrases.english: One must distance seeds, and the plow,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת מֵי רַגְלַיִם מִן הַכּוֹתֶל – שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.english: and urine, from the wall: three handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַזְּרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new group of items to the same list of distancing rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeds, a plow, and urine must be kept three טפחים from the wall.

steps.title: How far to keep a mill and an oven from the wall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a mill must be three טפחים from the lower stone, which equals four from the upper stone. An oven must be three טפחים from its base, which equals four from its rim.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one must keep a mill three handbreadths away measured from the lower stone, which is four from the upper stone. And an oven must be three handbreadths away measured from its base, which is four from its rim.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers a mill and an oven. It also tells us exactly where to measure the distance from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic distance is still three טפחים. The new detail is that a mill and an oven are wider at the bottom than at the top. So the משנה measures three טפחים from the wide lower part. Measured from the narrower top part, that same spot is four טפחים away.

keyTerms.meaning: The wide base of the oven
The narrow upper rim of the oven

steps.whatToRemember: Each item in this משנה has a set distance from the wall, usually three טפחים. For the mill and the oven, the three טפחים are counted from the wide bottom part. That works out to four טפחים from the narrower top part.
steps.confusionAlert: Three and four here are not two different rules. They describe the same distance, measured from two different parts of the item.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַרְחִיקִין אֶת הָרֵיחַיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁכֶב,
phrases.english: And one must distance the mill three handbreadths from the lower stone,
phrases.notes: The distance to the wall is measured starting from the bottom millstone.

phrases.english: which is four from the upper stone;
phrases.notes: The upper stone is smaller, so from its edge the same spot is four טפחים away.

phrases.english: and the oven, three from the base,
which is four from the rim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַרְחִיקִין אֶת הָרֵיחַיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁכֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list and adds where to measure from for items that are wider at the bottom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mill must be three טפחים from the lower stone, which is four from the upper stone. An oven must be three טפחים from its base, which is four from its rim.
